Thanks for the tag. Draft guidance below — this is intentionally non-legal. I've kept to high-level facts and avoided contractual language. Please do not publish the annotated DPA itself; point to the public subprocessor map and the DPA summary page.

Suggested 2-3 sentence blurb (for procurement packet):
"Redwood Inference acts as a data processor for Hosted API customers and processes customer-provided inputs only to fulfill inference requests. We retain transient request/response logs for up to 30 days for operational troubleshooting unless a customer configures a different retention policy; customer content is not used to train models. Data may be processed or stored by subprocessors and cloud providers in the United States and other jurisdictions necessary to provide service; we offer data residency options and contractual transfer mechanisms where required. A current list of subprocessors and our DPA overview are available at the link below."

Subprocessor confirmation: the attached subprocessor_map_2027-04-06.csv is current as of last week — that should satisfy procurement. For stricter regions (EU), point them to our DPA with SCCs / alternative transfer mechanisms.

If you want a single-sentence alternative for the packet intro, say so and I'll trim.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: short public-facing DPA summary for procurement packet

Nice draft, Laura — a couple of small product clarifications for the blurb so procurement doesn't get surprised:
- Retention: default logs retained up to 30 days; customers on Dedicated/Private can set retention to 0.
- Training: hosted API customer inputs are not used for training by default; we have an opt-in data sharing program for model improvements but it is explicitly consented to and documented separately.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a public subprocessor page; for procurement we typically provide the CSV snapshot and a link to the live page.

One-sentence option (marketing-friendly):
"Redwood processes customer inputs to deliver Hosted API inference; logs are retained short-term (typically up to 30 days), customer data is not used to train models by default, and a public list of subprocessors and data transfer practices is available."

I'll attach the subprocessor CSV and an internal annotated DPA that highlights the transfer and retention clauses.

Kimberly Park
Privacy & Product Counsel
Redwood Inference

Option A (2 sentences, neutral tone):
"Redwood acts as a processor for Hosted API customers and processes inputs only to provide inference. We keep operational logs short-term (typically up to 30 days), do not use customer inputs to train models by default, and maintain a public list of subprocessors and data transfer practices."

Option B (single-line, plain):
"Redwood processes your API requests to return model outputs; we retain logs for operational troubleshooting (usually up to 30 days), do not use your inputs to train models by default, and publish our subprocessors and transfer practices online."

Sara — if you tell me which option Acme prefers, I'll send a PNG and paste-ready text. Also linking the live subprocessor page and the DPA summary: https://www.redwood.com/privacy/dpa-summary and https://www.redwood.com/subprocessors
